everyday.prompt: Check the room and guest arrival time against S1, then the book limit and cancellation contact against S2. Rewrite any sentence that still carries the old invitation’s arrangements.
List confirmed guests, helpers, the reserved place and people still waiting separately. Trace each count to S2 or U1 before adding the people who can be in the room.
Calculate the upper bound for incoming books, table space and box space separately. Show where any overflow goes; do not turn the maximum into a promised quantity.
Compare your first and revised plans. Name what U1 changed and what stayed unchanged; explain why keeping correct reminder wording can be a valid revision decision.
Write the next reply-list check, who makes it and when. Explain what must be confirmed before the reserved place is offered to someone else.
Separate guest-facing arrangements from internal reply tracking. Keep the attendance decisions useful without putting individual reply details in the reminder.

work.prompt: Trace the slot, location and attendance to S2, readiness to S3, and unchanged commitments to S1. Correct only the facts that later notes actually replace.
Make the current slot, scope, owner and next decision easy to find. Replace a long retelling with a short update and a task/owner/timing list; keep missing dates explicit.
Show opening minutes plus sequential case minutes plus debrief minutes. Check both the available slot and ready cards before recommending a scope; label the timing as an estimate.
State the small outcome your recommendation would achieve and how you would check it. Keep a feasible recommendation distinct from an agreed decision; explain its tradeoff.
Keep your first update beside the revision. Point to each change supported by U1, explain the reason, and preserve commitments that U1 did not replace.
Mark the still-unknown meeting time and unobserved pilot results separately from known plans. Ask for the missing source before describing success or a new commitment.

technical.prompt: Match each expectation to its candidate: R1 replaces R0 for the supplied runs; R2 adds JPEG for the next candidate. Do not apply a later rule retroactively.
Give the next person the exact fixture type/bytes, build, steps, expected result and recorded actual result. Keep unsupported details from the vague support message as questions.
Use T01 for the observed UI mismatch, T02 for the successful control and T03 for an unconfirmed attempt. Keep the possible cause separate from a demonstrated finding.
Choose a matched browser/service check that can test the suspected limit. Include below, at and above the boundary and a recovery step if the response is interrupted.
Keep the initial investigation and original run IDs. Explain how R2 and D1 change the next plan while preserving what the earlier observations actually showed.
Label new checks not run. For an interrupted attempt, keep the expected result separate from the unknown actual outcome, and check request/storage state before deciding how to retry.
